sentences.text: Since there is a delay of 18 days in filing the present special appeal, which is nominal, we condone the same.
Delay condonation application is allowed.
SPECIAL APPEAL NO. 350 OF 2022 2) This special appeal is directed against the order dated 12.09.2022, passed by the learned Single Judge, in Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2232 of 2020.
The learned Single Judge has dismissed the writ petition preferred by the appellants.

SPA/350/2022 on 6 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105948631/
1 3)

The appellants have preferred the writ petition primarily to seek a mandamus against the respondents, not to take possession of the acquired land until respondent No. 1 CALA disburses the compensation, along with interest, in respect of the acquired land, admeasuring about 0.0050 and 0.0080 hectares, respectively.

Upon issuance of notice in the writ petition, respondent No. 2, i.e.,
the NHAI, filed its counter-affidavit disclosing that NHAI has already deposited the amount with CALA after adopting due process under the National Highways Act, and rules framed thereunder.

It was also stated that the competent authority of Land Acquisition (CALA) after adopting due process and approval under Section 3D of the National Highways Act had notified the land for acquisition.
4) After the objections preferred by the NHAI had been rejected by the Arbitrator on 11.09.2020,
objections under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act had been preferred by NHAI,
which are still pending.

5) It is in this background that the learned Single Judge held that there was no merit in the writ petition, since possession of the property has been taken over, at least in the record, which is also recognized as taking over of possession in law.
6) The submission of learned counsel for the appellants is that the appellants have not received the compensation.
Since compensation stands deposited by the NHAI, it is for the appellants to pursue their remedy for release of the same.
7) At this stage, counsel states that notice was issued by CALA to the erstwhile owner, who was no more.
It appears to us, that there is some issue which needs to be resolved with regard to the identity of the person to whom the compensation is to be released, as the heir of the recorded owner.
In these proceedings, we are not called upon to determine those issues.
8) We, therefore, dispose of this appeal leaving it open to the appellants to pursue their remedy for release of the compensation, in accordance with law.
9) Interim relief application (IA No. 01 of 2022) also stands disposed of.
________________ VIPIN SANGHI, C.J.

________________ RAKESH THAPLIYAL, J.
